A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MixFlow research work, with complete, readable main text and appendices across 23 pages. Equations, tables, figures, and renamed appendix sections can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original toy simulations, ImageNet generation experiments, SD 3.5 evaluations, and ablation studies.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and additionally reports Qwen-Image evaluations and a GVP training-target comparison.

M1.justification: Equation (9) changes the general velocity target from u*(x_t,t) to u*(x_m_t,m_t), while Section 5.2 retains the former as a GVP alternative. The revised RAE code samples m_t before timestep shifting and then shifts both timesteps, whereas v1 samples m_t after shifting t. These are localized revisions to the documented procedure; the central slowed-mixture approach remains.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the Gaussian toy task, ImageNet at 256 and 512 resolution, and text-to-image evaluation using GenEval, DPG-Bench, and T2I-CompBench. Qwen-Image adds a model within existing tasks. The newly named training-data sources document the previously described corpus without establishing a dataset change.

E2.justification: New Table F.1 compares MixFlow against Qwen-Image and its 10K-step and 20K-step conventional fine-tuning controls. Comparator membership in the retained ImageNet, exposure-bias, and SD 3.5 comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces evaluation of the 20B Qwen-Image model at 50 and 10 sampling steps, using 10K conventional fine-tuning steps followed by 10K MixFlow steps and a 20K conventional control. Section 5.2 also introduces the GVP target comparison at 500K versus 2500K training steps. The expanded metric listing describes metrics already used in v1.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds an analysis of GVP velocity-target choice, reporting equal performance after 500K versus 2500K training steps. Existing timestep-distribution, mixture-range, extra-training, and comparator-hyperparameter analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting and the min/max Slow Flow envelopes over 20,000 images remain unchanged.

E6.justification: SD 3.5 MixFlow scores are revised in Tables 7, D.4, and D.5: for example, 40-step GenEval changes from 0.66 to 0.69 and DPG-Bench from 86.16 to 87.49, without an explanation of the revisions. Table F.1 adds Qwen-Image results, including MixFlow GenEval scores of 0.90 and 0.86 at 50 and 10 steps. The GVP convergence finding is new; ImageNet results and existing qualitative samples are retained.

T1.justification: Equation (9) revises the mathematical definition of the loss target to the slowed timestep. This is substantive for time-varying GVP velocities, although linear-flow targets coincide. The Beta-sampling derivation and projection formula in Equation (12) are unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same Slow Flow motivation, MixFlow contribution, applicability claims, and headline ImageNet FID results. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds a speculative optimization explanation for the GVP target comparison, citing variation of the slowed-time velocity along the path. Appendix F interprets Qwen-Image results as evidence of applicability to larger models with different text encoders and RoPEs. Existing interpretations and applicability discussion are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly specifies 4.5M public-source and 0.5M synthetic training samples, source datasets, filtering/re-captioning models, and synthetic-image resolution. V2 also documents Qwen-Image training and revises the RAE code example. The revised snippet uses an unqualified time_dist_shift whose definition is not shown; access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds seven references supporting existing metrics and benchmarks, including GenEval, FID, T2I-CompBench, and precision/recall. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to exposure-bias methods are substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 updates authorship and affiliations, adds acknowledgments, expands several experimental explanations, and inserts a Qwen-Image appendix that shifts subsequent appendix lettering. Most prose and the main section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table F.1, relocates Figure 5 from page 9 to the text-to-image results on page 7, and revises the code display from Figure H.13 to I.13. Figure 1 adds initial 0.05 x-axis labels, with further spacing and layout adjustments. The sample galleries and existing analytical figures are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix D makes the previously unspecified text-to-image corpus more reproducible through concrete provenance and processing details. Appendix F adds architectural validation with an equal-training-budget Qwen-Image control. These provide a limited overall quality gain. The unexplained SD 3.5 score revisions and unresolved time_dist_shift reference in the revised code limit the improvement in reproducibility.
